instructions: The two clauses do not contradict. Does the changed clause reach into the linked clause's territory? Answer yes only when the linked clause states that a behavior, decision, or responsibility belongs to it or to a named owner, and the changed clause makes a different module, route, or spec do or decide that thing. Answer no for everything else.

labels.name: yes
labels.description: The changed clause extends into the scope or boundary the linked clause owns.

input.before: Reading view dims internal clauses in the browser.
input.after: Reading view changes provider thresholds on the server.
input.target: The browser runtime owns reading view and consumes the route.

input.after: The route edits the spec when a label is confident.
input.target: No suggestion edits a spec; only a human click writes.

input.after: The client computes each price's tax before showing it.
input.target: The billing service owns tax calculation; clients only display what it returns.

labels.name: no
labels.description: The changed clause stays in its own scope, restates the linked clause, extends it without crossing a boundary, belongs to another layer, is a sibling row of one table, names a Jev label word such as oversteps, or shares no boundary with the linked clause. An acceptance criterion, test, or user story about the linked clause's behavior is no.

input.before: The server stores one judgment record for each question.
input.target: The records are the cache: each is keyed by a hash of its question inputs and set version.

input.after: Given a saved filter, the toolbar lists it by name and choosing it applies it.
input.target: Saved filters appear in the toolbar list and apply when chosen.

input.after: As an operator on the Mac, I can install the plugin candidate for one exact PR SHA with one command, replacing whatever annotateanything build is installed.
input.target: One exact PR SHA becomes one immutable plugin candidate a human can install on the Mac BB app, smoke, and remove with one receipt.

input.after: As an operator, the Factory page opens without waiting for a fresh /lanes read: it shows the fleet as last read at once, then catches up, and never blanks.
input.target: The page opens from its open snapshot, then reads /lanes once the floor is ready and every 5 seconds after; each read that changes a lane adds a move to the timeline.
